text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Thailand to get IMF shock treatment with reforms to financial institutions, higher value added tax and budget measures in return for $12-15 billion in emergency loans.
-- The dollar hits new high above 1.88 marks and 6.35 francs despite concerns expressed by Bundesbank chief economist Ottmar Issing.
-- Jeff Medlock, head of the six-country Eureko insurance group which is a bidder in the privatisation of GAN, wants to create a multinational quoted company with the French insurer.
-- GEC Alsthom and Framatome confirm their interest in Westinghouse's energy activities but the U.S. conglomerate has not followed up their interest.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Canal Plus and the Amaury press group are preparing a news channel, with an agreement expected in September and a launch next spring.

-- White-collar workers concerned over measures for the 35-hour week which could lead to pay cuts without reductions in working time. The CGC union wants the measures spelled out, while strong opposition from the metallurgical and mining union worries the government.

-- An agreement between the French AFNOR standards organisation and International Handling Services of the United States is being studied by the French national audit office and competition authorities of the European Commission.
L'AGEFI
-- Monetary authorities on both sides of the Atlantic concerned over the dollar's rise.
-- Some French companies face difficulties due to the dollar's appreciation, particularly exporters who had counted on a dollar below six francs and importers whose currency cover was too narrow.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- The European Union's agricultural policy is too complex and needs to be simplified, said Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Concerns over the dollar rise and mark weakness.
-- GEC Alsthom and Framatome confirm interest in Westinghouse energy units.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Dollar hits eight-year high against the mark.
-- Thai government commits to austerity policy and will close down finance companies to qualify for IMF credit line.
